sqli.title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
sqli.description: An attacker can append or inject SQL commands into an application's input parameters, leading to unauthorized read/write access to the database or execution of administrative commands.

xss.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
xss.description: An attacker injects malicious scripts into trusted websites, which are then executed by the victim's browser, leading to session hijacking, defacement, or redirection.

ssrf.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
ssrf.description: The web application fetches a remote resource without validating the user-supplied URL, allowing an attacker to coerce the application to send crafted requests to internal or external systems.

ssti.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
ssti.description: An attacker injects malicious input into a template, which is executed on the server by the template engine, potentially leading to remote code execution (RCE).

idor.title: Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR)
idor.description: An application provides direct access to objects based on user-supplied input, allowing attackers to bypass authorization and access other users' data by modifying the identifier.

csrf.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
csrf.description: An attacker forces an authenticated user's browser to send a forged HTTP request, including session cookies, to execute unauthorized actions on behalf of the victim.

mass_assignment.title: Mass Assignment
mass_assignment.description: The application automatically binds user-supplied input parameters to internal model attributes or variables without filtering, allowing attackers to modify restricted properties.

graphql.title: GraphQL Security Issues
graphql.description: Vulnerabilities specific to GraphQL endpoints, such as introspection abuse, excessive query depth/complexity leading to denial of service, or improper field-level authorization.

jwt_abuse.title: JSON Web Token (JWT) Abuse
jwt_abuse.description: Weak cryptographic signatures, support for the 'none' algorithm, insecure key storage, key confusion attacks, or lack of signature verification that allows attackers to forge or manipulate JWT tokens.

rce.title: Remote Code Execution (RCE)
rce.description: An attacker can execute arbitrary commands or code on the host operating system of the target application, leading to complete system compromise.

lfi.title: Local File Inclusion (LFI)
lfi.description: An application includes a local file based on user input without proper validation, allowing attackers to read sensitive local files or execute code if paired with log poisoning or file upload.

xxe.title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
xxe.description: An application processes XML input containing references to external entities, allowing attackers to read internal files, perform port scans, or initiate SSRF attacks.

deserialization.title: Insecure Deserialization
deserialization.description: The application deserializes untrusted data without verification, allowing an attacker to manipulate object state and execute arbitrary code, bypass access controls, or cause denial of service.

oauth2.title: OAuth 2.0 Security Flaws
oauth2.description: Improper validation of redirect URIs, state parameters (CSRF), token leakage, scope escalation, or client credential exposure in OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization flows.

broken_access_control.title: Broken Access Control
broken_access_control.description: Failure to restrict access to resources, allowing unauthorized users to perform administrative tasks, read confidential data, or modify other users' settings.

bola.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
bola.description: Vulnerability in API design where the server does not validate if the logged-in user has permission to access a specific object using its identifier.

authentication_weakness.title: Authentication Weakness
authentication_weakness.description: Flaws in credential management, lack of multi-factor authentication, support for weak password policies, or vulnerability to credential stuffing and brute force.

sca_vuln.title: Software Composition Analysis (SCA) Vulnerability
sca_vuln.description: Use of outdated third-party libraries, modules, or dependencies containing known security vulnerabilities (CVEs).

container_vuln.title: Container Security Vulnerability
container_vuln.description: Misconfigurations or security flaws in container images (Docker, OCI), rootless policy violations, container escapes, or insecure Docker socket exposure.

active_directory.title: Active Directory Security Issues
active_directory.description: Common AD misconfigurations and attack vectors including Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, DCSync/DCShadow, trust abuse, and insecure GPO settings.

cloud_vuln.title: Cloud Security Issues
cloud_vuln.description: Overly permissive IAM roles, publicly accessible storage buckets, insecure instance metadata services (IMDS), or misconfigured VPC firewall rules.

osint_leak.title: OSINT Information Leakage
osint_leak.description: Exposure of sensitive company credentials, API keys, intellectual property, or architectural diagrams on public repositories, paste sites, or search engines.

network_anomaly.title: Network Traffic Anomaly
network_anomaly.description: Suspicious or unexpected traffic patterns indicating unauthorized port scanning, C2 beaconing, DNS tunneling, or data exfiltration.

lateral_movement.title: Lateral Movement
lateral_movement.description: Techniques used by adversaries to access and control remote systems on an internal network (e.g. SMB execution, WMI, RDP session hijacking).

privilege_escalation.title: Privilege Escalation
privilege_escalation.description: Adversaries attempt to gain higher-level permissions on a system or network by exploiting security vulnerabilities, design flaws, or misconfigurations.

subdomain_enum.title: Subdomain Enumeration
subdomain_enum.description: The gathering of subdomain records belonging to a target domain, which maps the external attack surface and exposes hidden interfaces.

subdomain_takeover.title: Subdomain Takeover
subdomain_takeover.description: An attacker registers a domain name referenced by a target organization's DNS alias (CNAME), gaining control of requests sent to that subdomain.

exposed_secret.title: Exposed Secret / Credentials
exposed_secret.description: Hardcoded API keys, private keys, database passwords, or auth tokens found in source code, configuration files, or build artifacts.

race_condition.title: Race Condition
race_condition.description: A concurrency issue where the system's execution sequence depends on the relative timing of events, allowing attackers to bypass rate limits or transaction locks.

request_smuggling.title: HTTP Request Smuggling
request_smuggling.description: Discrepancies in how front-end and back-end servers interpret Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers, allowing attackers to inject requests into user sessions.

vuln_scan.title: Vulnerability Scanning Target
vuln_scan.description: Generic system, network, or service target configured to undergo automated vulnerability scanning.

graphql_security.title: GraphQL Security Evaluation
graphql_security.description: Assessment of a GraphQL service's endpoints for vulnerability to injection, authorization bypass, and resource exhaustion.

serverless_security.title: Serverless Security Flaws
serverless_security.description: Vulnerabilities in ephemeral cloud functions (Lambda, Cloud Functions) including insecure event parameters, excessive IAM permissions, or secret leakage.

kubernetes_security.title: Kubernetes Security Vulnerability
kubernetes_security.description: Misconfigured pod security policies, open etcd endpoints, API server exposure, or weak RBAC policies within a Kubernetes cluster.

mobile_security.title: Mobile Application Security Vulnerability
mobile_security.description: Security flaws in iOS or Android applications, such as insecure local data storage, poor transit security, binary tampering, or intent injection.

incident_response.title: Incident Response Indicator
incident_response.description: Security event or signal indicating active intrusion, data exfiltration, ransomware encryption, or workstation compromise.

threat_hunting.title: Threat Hunting Hypothesis
threat_hunting.description: Proactive investigation scenario targeted at uncovering undetected attacker activity across the network or system logs.

forensics.title: Forensic Analysis Target
forensics.description: System memory dump, disk image, or log file to be parsed for digital artifacts and timeline reconstruction.

sast_sink.title: SAST Vulnerability Sink
sast_sink.description: Dangerous API call or code pattern identified by Static Application Security Testing that receives untrusted source input (e.g. exec, eval, innerHTML).
